Account help: Use your VELUX ACTIVE account. You can sign in with email and password or supply a refresh token. The adapter uses the cloud even after local gateway pairing.
Refresh token help: A supplied refresh token is used for token authentication. Leave empty to sign in with email and password. Password, refresh token and client secret are encrypted by ioBroker.
OAuth client help: Normally leave both client fields empty. Only enter a matching client ID and client secret if you use your own compatible OAuth client.
Events help: Connect to the cloud event stream for faster updates. Regular polling remains enabled and provides a fallback when the stream is unavailable.
Poll interval help: Default: 60 seconds. Minimum: 15 seconds. Very short intervals increase cloud requests.
Gateway pairing help: For signed commands, assign the original gateway ID from the object data to its local IP address or hostname. The ioBroker host must reach this gateway over the local network. A configured address alone does not create a key.
Pairing steps: Save these settings. Set homes.<home>.gateways.<gateway>.pairing.start to true. Wait for the gateway LED to blink and press its physical button. Only then set pairing.confirm to true to retrieve the keys. Follow pairing.status in Objects; pairing.cancel aborts the process. Keys are stored encrypted internally; there is no key field to fill in here.
Individual stop help: Enables the device stop command using target_position = -1. This individual command has not been confirmed in the examined app or on hardware. The proven stopAll command stops all movements at the selected gateway and is available independently.
Force commands help: Add force=true to movement commands. Keep disabled unless it is required for your setup; cloud or gateway safety restrictions may still apply.
Raw data help: Publish additional cloud response data as JSON for diagnosis. These data can contain home, room and device identifiers. Pairing keys and authentication tokens must remain private.
